chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan — from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'The dyeing of God, and who is better than God in dyeing?' He said: 'It is Islam.'
And he said regarding His words, Mighty and Majestic: 'He has indeed grasped the firmest handle,' he said: 'It is faith in God alone, with no associate for Him.'

key_terms.الْإِيمَان بِاللَّه وَحْدَه: Belief in God alone — the pure tawhid without any association
key_terms.الْعُرْوَة الْوُثْقى: The Firmest Handle — Quranic phrase (2:256) interpreted as tawhid, the belief in God's absolute oneness
key_terms.صِبْغَة: Dyeing/coloring — the Quranic term alluding to Christian baptism (sibgha), reinterpreted as the divine imprinting of Islam on the soul

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say is meant by 'the dyeing of God' and 'the firmest handle' in the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets two Quranic verses for his companion Abdullah ibn Sinan. He explains that 'the dyeing of God' in Quran 2:138 — a reference to baptism as practiced by Christians, which the Quran transforms into the concept of divine imprinting — refers to Islam as the true divine coloring of the human soul. He further explains that 'the firmest handle' in Quran 2:256 signifies pure tawhid: belief in God alone with absolutely no associates. These explanations reflect the Imami tradition of authoritative Quranic interpretation, where the Imam's explanation carries doctrinal weight.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:138] A Dyeing of Allah, and who is better than Allah in dyeing? Heasws said: ‘Al-Islām’.

And heasws said regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [2:256] he indeed has grabbed hold on the Firmest Handle, heasws said: ‘It is the Emān (belief) in Allahazwj Alone, there being no associates for Himazwj’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, ‘. . . It is the coloring of Allah. Who has a better color than Allah’s color?’ [2:138], abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘Color is a reference to this belief.’ The Imam also said, ‘It (color) stands for al-Islam.’

In the words of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, ‘. . . He has established a firm hold onto the strong ring’. . . [2:256], he said, ‘It (the strong ring) is a reference to the faith and belief in Allah, Who is One and has no partners.’”
